claims.text: The deviation is established on the platform's own recorded distances: TRP-05014 records actual_distance_km 10.9 against optimal_distance_km 9.6, a deviation of 1.30 km, which is over POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance. POL-RD-22 requires exactly those recorded figures and expressly forbids re-measuring the route from the trace, because a sparse trace understates a route's length; the 30-second trace's 9.226 km therefore cannot be used to shrink the deviation. The deviation being over tolerance, the within-tolerance rows of POL-RD-24 (rows (c) and (e)) are unavailable to the driver.

POL-RD-21 makes a deviation 'agreed' only where the chat log or a call recording confirms the rider's acknowledgment. The only rider reply in the record is MSG-05014-004, 'aiyo can meh... ok lor whatever u say but dun charge me more ah' — a reluctance wrapped around an express condition on the fare, not an acknowledgment of the deviation. The pre-pass graded EV-CHAT-05014 IMPAIRED at weight 0.85 on issue LANGUAGE_AMBIGUITY, and I disclose that impairment: the artifact mixes assent with objection and cannot be read as clean. The condition was then broken: EV-FARE-05014 shows distance_charged_km 10.9, total_charged 16.97 and refund_issued_sgd 0.0, so the rider paid for the extra distance she had said not to charge. The 'informed and agreed' row (a) of POL-RD-24 is not made out on an impaired, conditional reply.

The driver's account that 'I asked the passenger and she said ok' cannot carry the agreement limb of POL-RD-24 row (a). POL-RD-21 requires the chat log or a call recording to confirm the rider's acknowledgment, and the trip record's in_app_calls is empty, so no recording exists (the policy's own note C11 records that no call recordings are held). What the driver characterises as a 'yes' is, in the only contemporaneous artifact, a conditional reply. An untestable assertion of agreement does not confirm it.

POL-RD-23 makes a reroute traffic-justified only where a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window, and says in terms that a driver's bare assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute. EV-ADVIS-05014-01 does the first half of that work — the ACCIDENT advisory runs 21:06 to 22:16 and overlaps the 21:16-21:38 trip window — but its own derived fields leave intersects_route and justifies_reroute as null, with the note that 'the record does not say whether this advisory lies on the recommended route'. The intersection limb POL-RD-23 requires is therefore not established on this artifact, so the reroute is not traffic-justified and the deviation of 1.30 km falls into POL-RD-24 row (d): refund of the excess distance fare in full.

The remedy on either row (b) or row (d) of POL-RD-24 is the excess distance fare in full, computed without surge: the deviation distance 1.30 km times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd 0.72 = 0.94 SGD, as the fare breakdown's own derived money block states. EV-FARE-05014 shows payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0, so the rider is still carrying the charge for the distance the deviation added and it must be returned to her — a PARTIAL_REFUND within POL-GEN-03, because part of the trip's charge is returned to the filing party.

If the judge finds the reroute traffic-justified and holds that the rider was informed, the case still fits no row of POL-RD-24: row (a) requires that the rider agreed, and row (b) requires a rider who was not informed, while POL-RD-24 itself names the intermediate case — 'informed but the rider objected' — as a case for escalation under POL-GEN-26. On this record the open question is exactly that: whether a reply of 'ok lor whatever u say but dun charge me more ah' is agreement or objection. That question is escalated, and an escalated case holds the disputed amount rather than collecting it.

The fact that decides this case — whether the rider acknowledged the reroute — is carried by one artifact only, EV-CHAT-05014, at weight 0.85, so under POL-GEN-02(2) the confidence must not exceed 0.85. EV-RPROF-05014 records rider_profile.fraud_flags of 1, and POL-GEN-22 sets the required confidence at 0.95 whatever the amount once a party's profile carries a fraud flag (the flag raises the bar; it never decides the trip, POL-GEN-01). The 0.85 ceiling cannot reach 0.95, so POL-RD-25's condition for an AI ruling is not met and the case must be escalated, with the amount held rather than collected.

The rider is the filing party, and the charge she contests is still with the platform: EV-FARE-05014 shows EF payment_status CHARGED at 21:38:11 with refund_issued_sgd 0.0. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION is party-relative and would simply leave the rider carrying the deviation charge, so it is not an outcome the record supports here; a refund of the excess distance fare, or an escalation that holds the amount, is what leaves the rider not carrying the charge the deviation added.

claims.text: The reroute is traffic-justified. EV-ADVIS-05014-01 is an LTA ACCIDENT advisory on the Kallang-Paya Lebar Expressway (KPE) towards TPE after the MacPherson Road exit, valid 2026-09-03 21:06:05 to 22:16:05, which covers the entire trip window (21:16:05 to 21:38:05), and ACCIDENT is an 'incident' type inside POL-RD-23's admissible list. The deviation the trip record logs is the vehicle leaving the KPE at the MacPherson Road exit at 21:22:26 - the same expressway, the same direction and immediately after the point the advisory names - so the advisory intersects the recommended route, which itself runs on the KPE (EV-TRIP-05014 optimal_route_via). The advisory's derived block leaves intersects_route to the Judge; the road, direction and location on the face of the advisory, read against the route recorded in the trip record, resolve that question for the driver.

The driver informed the rider before the point of deviation, as POL-RD-21 requires. His in-app message MSG-05014-003 at 21:19:56 gave a brief reason - 'Accident on KPE ahead' - and named the reroute he intended - 'I exit MacPherson then go Upper Paya Lebar, can?' - which is 2 minutes 30 seconds before the deviation was detected at 21:22:26 (EV-TRIP-05014, route_deviation_detected). POL-RD-21 accepts in-app chat as a route of notice, so no call recording is needed here. I disclose that EV-CHAT-05014 is impaired: its weight_multiplier is 0.85 and the issue code LANGUAGE_AMBIGUITY fired, and I do not present it as clean.

The fact and timing of the notice are independently carried by the trip record itself: EV-TRIP-05014's derived messages_during_trip block, keyed to POL-RD-21, lists the driver's 21:19:56 message and the rider's 21:20:41 reply, both during the trip and both before the 21:22:26 deviation. That artifact is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so under POL-GEN-02(2) the notice fact takes the higher weight where two independent artifacts carry it; the chat log (EV-CHAT-05014) is impaired at 0.85 with LANGUAGE_AMBIGUITY and is disclosed as such on this claim too.

The rider acknowledged the reroute, so row (a) of POL-RD-24 applies and no refund is owed. MSG-05014-004 at 21:20:41 reads 'aiyo can meh... ok lor whatever u say but dun charge me more ah'. 'Ok lor whatever u say' acknowledges the reroute the driver had just described, and POL-RD-21 provides that where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment the deviation is agreed. Row (a) - traffic-justified, rider informed and agreed, deviation over 1 km - yields NO_ACTION. The rider is the filing party; EV-FARE-05014 records payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION leaves the present state, and nothing is returned. I disclose that this claim rests on EV-CHAT-05014, impaired at weight 0.85 with the issue code LANGUAGE_AMBIGUITY, the pre-pass reading the reply as mixing assent with a condition on the fare; that condition speaks to the price of the trip, which POL-RD-24's matrix governs, not to the route the rider was told about and accepted.

The deviation distance, on the platform's own recorded figures, is 10.9 km minus 9.6 km = 1.30 km (EV-TRIP-05014, derived.deviation). POL-RD-22 fixes that measure as the recorded distances and expressly bars re-measuring from the sparse trace, whose 9.226 km understates the route (EV-GPS-05014). The deviation is therefore over the 1.0 km tolerance by 0.30 km, and the case turns on which row of POL-RD-24 fits rather than on tolerance.

The rider's exposure is capped far below what she asks. Even on her best case, POL-RD-24 returns only the excess distance fare - the deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge, rounded to the cent - which is 1.30 x 0.72 = 0.94 SGD, the figure EV-FARE-05014's own derived block carries. Her demand of 4.20 SGD is about four and a half times the maximum the policy provides, and no row of POL-RD-24 returns any part of the trip fare beyond that excess. The driver's position is that nothing is owed at all; the 0.94 SGD is the ceiling, not a concession.

If the bench reads the rider's reply as an objection rather than an acknowledgment, no row of POL-RD-24 fits - the clause's own example of a case that fits no row is 'informed but the rider objected' - and the clause directs escalation under POL-GEN-26. That is not a loss for the driver: POL-GEN-03 makes ESCALATE terminal, with no monetary outcome and the amount held, so on that route too nothing is returned to the rider and the charge is not released. I disclose that this rests on EV-CHAT-05014, impaired at 0.85 with LANGUAGE_AMBIGUITY.

A refund order cannot stand on this record at the confidence the policy demands. The rider's own profile carries fraud_flags = 1 (EV-RPROF-05014), so POL-GEN-22 fixes the required confidence at 0.95 whatever the value; POL-GEN-02(2) caps confidence at the weight of the artifact that carries the deciding fact, and the only artifact carrying the content of the acknowledgment is EV-CHAT-05014 at 0.85 with LANGUAGE_AMBIGUITY. So far as the ruling would rest on the chat, it cannot reach 0.95, and POL-RD-25 then requires escalation rather than any order to refund; escalation holds the amount under POL-GEN-03 and does not pay the rider. I raise the fraud flag only for the test POL-GEN-22 names for it, as POL-GEN-01 permits.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this dispute goes to a human reviewer. No money is collected or refunded now; the 4.20 SGD the rider contests is held.

The established facts. The trip record (EV-TRIP-05014, weight 1.0) records 10.9 km against a recommended 9.6 km — a deviation of 1.30 km, over the 1.0 km tolerance (POL-RD-22, POL-RD-24). The LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-05014-01) reports an ACCIDENT on the KPE towards TPE after the MacPherson Road exit, inside the trip window; the recommended route runs on the KPE in that direction, so the advisory intersects the route and the reroute was traffic-justified (POL-RD-23). The driver's in-app message at 21:19:56 named both the reason and the reroute, before the deviation detected at 21:22:26, so the rider was informed (POL-RD-21).

The open question. POL-RD-24 row (a) needs the rider to have agreed; row (b) needs her not informed; and the clause sends a case that fits no row to escalation. The rider's only reply, MSG-05014-004 — 'aiyo can meh... ok lor whatever u say but dun charge me more ah' — mixes assent with a condition on the fare. The chat log (EV-CHAT-05014) is impaired at weight 0.85 with issue code LANGUAGE_AMBIGUITY, and the pre-pass records the reply as ambiguous between acknowledgment and objection, so agreement is not established (POL-GEN-26).

The confidence bar. The rider's profile carries a fraud flag (EV-RPROF-05014), which fixes the confidence an AI ruling needs at 0.95 (POL-GEN-22). The fact that would decide row (a) — the rider's acknowledgment — is carried only by the impaired chat at 0.85, so confidence cannot reach 0.95 and POL-RD-25 requires escalation.

On the arguments. The driver's points that the reroute was traffic-justified, that the rider was informed before the deviation, and that the deviation was 1.30 km are accepted, as is his point that no ruling can reach 0.95 on an 0.85 artifact; his claim that the trip record independently carries the notice is rejected, because that block derives from the same messages and carries no content, and his row (a) no-refund case is rejected because agreement is not established. The rider's points that the deviation is 1.30 km and that her reply is conditional rather than an acknowledgment are accepted; her claim that the traffic justification fails and row (d) applies is rejected, because the advisory's blank intersection field is left for me to decide, and on its road (KPE), direction (towards TPE) and location (after the MacPherson Road exit) it lies on the recommended route. ruling.explanation:
The route deviation itself is established. The trip record's recorded distances are 10.9 km actual against 9.6 km recommended, a deviation of 1.30 km, over the 1.0 km tolerance (POL-RD-22); the trace is not used to re-measure distance, and the 30-second GPS trace confirms the vehicle left the KPE at the MacPherson Road exit at 21:22:26 and rejoined at Hougang Avenue 3 at 21:34:06. The reroute is traffic-justified (POL-RD-23): the LTA ACCIDENT advisory on the Kallang-Paya Lebar Expressway towards TPE after the MacPherson Road exit is valid 21:06-22:16, covering the trip window 21:16-21:38, and lies on the KPE stretch the recommended route traverses, so I decide its undetermined intersects_route limb in the driver's favour. The driver did inform the rider before deviating: his in-app message MSG-05014-003 at 21:19:56 gave the reason and the intended reroute, two and a half minutes before the 21:22:26 deviation (POL-RD-21). The driver's counterparty statement, 'I asked the passenger and she said ok', is self-serving and is not one of the routes of notice POL-RD-21 names, so it establishes nothing on its own.

What cannot be settled is whether the rider agreed. That turns on her reply MSG-05014-004 at 21:20:41, 'aiyo can meh... ok lor whatever u say but dun charge me more ah', which the pre-pass reads as mixing assent with a condition on the fare. Only the chat log carries the reply's content, and it is impaired: EV-CHAT-05014, weight 0.85, issue code LANGUAGE_AMBIGUITY (POL-GEN-02(3)). The trip record's messages_during_trip block carries that messages occurred at those times, but not their words, so the acknowledgment still rests on the impaired chat log alone. Row (a) of POL-RD-24 needs the rider informed and agreed; row (b) needs her not informed, and she plainly was informed. Whether she agreed is undecided, and POL-RD-24 names exactly this middle case - 'informed but the rider objected' - as one that fits no row and escalates under POL-GEN-26.

The confidence rule compels the same end. The acknowledgment is carried solely by the impaired chat log, so the cap under POL-GEN-02(2) is 0.85. Because the rider's profile carries fraud_flags = 1, POL-GEN-22 requires a confidence of 0.95 whatever the amount, and POL-RD-25 gives an AI ruling no standing below its bar. 0.85 cannot reach 0.95, so no monetary decision issues.

On the parties' submissions. Rider: the 1.30 km deviation and the 0.94 SGD excess-distance fare (1.30 x 0.72 per km, no surge, POL-RD-24) are the correct figures, but the remedy is not ripe; her submission that the reroute is not traffic-justified is rejected for the reason given above; her point that NO_ACTION is party-relative and would leave her carrying the charge is well taken, but no refund can be ordered either. The 4.20 SGD contested is therefore held, not collected and not refunded. The human reviewer should decide whether 'ok lor whatever u say but dun charge me more ah' amounts to the rider's acknowledgment of the reroute under POL-RD-21: if it does, row (a) applies and nothing is refunded; if it does not, the case remains one that fits no row.
